Char'li's body burned, fire coursing through his veins scorching his nerves as an ocean of life flowed all about him. How easy it would be he thought, to give in to the fire, to be consumed and float freely within the ocean for eternity, to leave the troubles of the mortal world behind. As Char'li struggled against the fire's pull the words of his teachers echoed in his mind "Deep breaths, long and calm. Remember the movements, channel the flame, direct it and control."

Five years had passed since Char'li, son of Dae'el had emerged from the nightmare of the Burrows, the spark of an unknown power burning within. He had learned and experienced much in this time but now a journey was beginning, one that would take him further than any Med'ja had travelled before. But before we look to the future we must look to the past to see how it is our hero arrived at this conjunction.....

----

After emerging from the Burrows Char'li and Sha'ne had needed time to recuperate for their time underground had left them weak. During this time Char'li remained among his kin in their new home but as his strength grew so did the spark. A dull persistent heat within and the pressure of life pressing down from all around had forced the young Med'ja to seek help from the elders, lest he be driven mad, yet for all their knowledge they could provide no relief. suggested he seek out her brothers at the Great Tree for among their kind there were none more knowledgeable than the Shamans of Umbralocht.

North and West Char'li Travelled in desperation by foot and by cart until a week had passed and he at last found himself standing beneath the bough of the Great Tree.

Here too his power was unknown but where the Elders would accept failure the shamans could not, probing, experimenting, researching until at last the source of Char'li's pain was revealed. Char'li himself was the greatest source of information regaling the Shamans with the tale of his escape and the Chieftains magic. Together however they quickly came to some interesting conclusions: Firstly though obviously magical in nature it appeared there was an actual flame burning within the young Med'ja, for the intensity of the burning would grow in the presence of a gale of breeze, Secondly that the pressure Char'li felt around him was somehow connected to the amount of living beings in his presence and had a range of some 50 metres, the smaller the population around him the lesser the pressure and so too did the flame shrink until at last Char'li's pain began to ease.

Cloistered away within the uppermost reaches of the Great Tree Char'li had at last found peace of mind. But now that the nature of his power was known there was the issue of how to control it and once he had, if he could, what would he become? Would he be driven to madness and corruption like the Chieftan? Or would the flame merely consume and turn his flesh to ash?

The answer to his dilemma arrived scant days after the nature of his power was known, not from the brotherhood but from their kin, the tall green Flora that had come to reside at the base of the great tree. Kuo Bo, an old male Flora had come to the Shamans to share his wisdom: To the Flora the flame was a signal of some internal conflict, an unbalancing of body and soul the pain of which could only be cured by re-alignment. In an age long passed when the touch of the God of change first appeared among their kind many Flora had developed a ritual, a series of movements performed in conjunction with the control of breath to calm the storm of their mind and bring it back into alignment with their soul.

This ritual, known only to the Flora was now offered To Char'li, but in return he would be required to study the works of the brotherhood and to work alongside the Flora to aide them in the propagation of their garden, this too they claimed, would help align his body and soul as it would strengthen both his body and mind and nurture his soul. With the chance to once again reclaim his future hanging before him Char'li accepted the Flora's offer and his training began.

For many weeks Char'li remained within the upper reaches of the Great Tree as the old Flora assisted in building his resistance to the pain of the fire and the strain of the pressure bearing down on him, his days filled with pain, sweat and exhaustion. Weeks became turned into months and slowly but surely Char'li was able to ventured ever closer to he lowest reaches of the Great Tree and the classrooms of the Brotherhood.

One day, some 14 months after his ascension of the tree Char'li found himself standing before a vibrant garden, the blue sky stretching on endlessly above as a cool breeze rustled the leaves of the Great Tree. "Now", the Flora said "Your teaching begins"
